articles.headline: Hits & Misses: Liverpool clicking and Chelsea get serious
keyFacts: Liverpool secured a 2-1 victory against nine-man Brentford, showing encouraging signs from their expensive attacking signings Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, and Bradley Barcola.
Chelsea earned a 2-0 win at Everton, securing their first league clean sheet under manager Xabi Alonso and their first in nine months.
Fulham defeated Hull to lift themselves out of the relegation zone, buying under-pressure manager Alvaro Arbeloa time after a winless start to the season.
body: Premier League hits and misses: Liverpool ride their luck to win at Brentford
Sky Sports' football writers analyse Saturday's Premier League action as Chelsea win at Everton and Liverpool beat nine-man Brentford...
Saturday 17 October 2026 19:09, UK
Liverpool spent close to £400m on Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola. Against Brentford, there was evidence that expensively-assembled attack might finally be clicking.

Isak was on the fringes of the game for long periods, limited to only 16 touches by the dogged hosts. But his brilliantly-taken goal, controlled and rifled home with dizzying speed in the second half, was a reminder of just how deadly he can be at his best.

It took him to five goals for the season. Only Erling Haaland has scored more in the Premier League. He is putting a difficult first season behind him and Andoni Iraola will be encouraged that it was Barcola who provided the assist.

The France international came into the game off the back of scoring a hat-trick against LASK in midweek and while he couldn't find the net against Brentford, missing a golden opportunity in the first half and hitting the bar in the second, Iraola liked what he saw.
"I love that he's having so many chances and being in those situations," said the Liverpool boss.
Then there was Wirtz, who provided the assist for Victor Munoz with a perfectly-weighted through-ball.
It was one of nine chances created - the joint-most by any Liverpool player in a single game since Opta started taking records in 2003/04.
Nick Wright

Chelsea have the best front three in the Premier League but attack being the best form of defence for Xabi Alonso was never going to be sustainable. No team had conceded more goals than Chelsea's 13 after six Premier League matches.

But, in Saturday's 2-0 victory at Everton, they showed a different side to their game. Remarkably, this was not only Alonso's first clean sheet in the league since his appointment but also Chelsea's first clean sheet in the league for nine months.

Defensively, Chelsea have been a liability for some time. Alonso must fix that if his team are to take the leap and challenge again. The win at Everton was a step in the right direction. In the manager's words, Chelsea produced a "serious" and "mature" performance.

These are the characteristics that will differentiate Chelsea from most of the chasing pack in a Premier League season where seriousness is sorely lacking among some of the so-called 'Big Six'. Alonso, clearly, is a serious manager.
Zinny Boswell
An ominous stat was provided by Opta during the build-up to Brentford's clash with Liverpool at the Gtech.
"Since their promotion to the top flight in 2021, the Bees have dropped more points from winning positions than any other side in the Premier League (102)."
A surprise, perhaps, given the Bees have taken to the top flight so well and finished in the top half in three of their first five seasons. And one that poses the question: what could have been?
For Brentford fans, that will not bear thinking about.
But that figure increased to 105 on Saturday, as they took the lead against the Reds before falling to a 2-1 defeat in a game they ended with nine men on the pitch.

Without the first of those reds - shown to Yehor Yarmoliuk before half-time, it might have been different. The reality? It's 11 points dropped for the season now, more than any other team in the division.
It has become a horrible habit - and one that needs kicking in to touch by Keith Andrews' men if those European ambitions are to materialise.
Dan Long
Could this be the turning point in Alvaro Arbeloa's Fulham reign?
It is certainly a start. With reports suggesting the Spaniard had two games to save his job, he needed a response and his players delivered one.
Fulham played with an intensity and attacking fluency that had been missing during their winless start to the Premier League season.

They registered 10 first-half shots, moved the ball quickly and repeatedly exposed a Hull side who struggled to impose themselves. Alex Iwobi's goal was deserved, but the hosts could easily have won by a greater margin.
There were encouraging signs of an identity taking shape, with the performance even prompting thoughts of 'Arbeloa-ball' at Craven Cottage.
Yet one result cannot erase the concerns of the opening weeks, and Fulham made the closing stages unnecessarily nervy before Ryan Sessegnon's stoppage-time red card.
The win lifts them out of the relegation zone and gives Arbeloa breathing space.
Whether it proves a turning point depends on what follows. For now, he has bought himself time and shown what his Fulham side can be.
William Bitibiri

articles.headline: Jacquet was 'cute and clever' for his part in Yarmoliuk red - Andrews
keyFacts: Brentford head coach Keith Andrews stated that Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet was clever in his role during Yehor Yarmoliuk's red card.
Yarmoliuk was sent off just before half-time for a headbutting action against Jacquet during Liverpool's 2-1 victory.
Goals from Victor Munoz and Alexander Isak secured the win for Liverpool after Yarmoliuk's dismissal changed the match dynamics.
body: Brentford: Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet was 'cute and clever' for his part in Yehor Yarmoliuk's red card

Brentford took the lead through Keane Lewis-Potter at the Gtech Community Stadium, but Yehor Yarmoliuk's red card before half-time changed the game; "If you look at where Jacquet is walking, he's not looking at the ball, is he? He's walking in to Yarmo" - Bees boss Keith Andrews
Saturday 17 October 2026 19:04, UK
Brentford head coach Keith Andrews felt Jeremy Jacquet was "cute and clever" for his role in Yehor Yarmoliuk's red card in the 2-1 defeat to Liverpool.

Ukraine international Yarmoliuk was sent off in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time at the Gtech Community Stadium for catching Jacquet with what referee John Brooks called - after going to the VAR monitor - "a headbutting action".
The Reds defender went to ground in the box - but Andoni Iraola's men were not awarded a penalty as a corner on the left-hand side had not yet been delivered.

"We need to look at ourselves first, which we always do. We don't really tend to look at what part they played within the incident," said Andrews in his post-match press conference.
"I do think they were cute, clever - but Yarmo needs to do better, so I can understand why it was a red."
Asked what he meant, Andrews clarified: "If you look at where Jacquet is walking, he's not looking at the ball, is he? He's walking in to Yarmo."
A further follow-up asked if he felt Jacquet made the most of the contact.
"We focus on us and our actions within that and you can make up your own mind," he added.
"Yarmo is an amazing young man. I think we need to remember he is young, very young, and he is someone who we love working with and trying to develop. He will learn from it."
Goals from Victor Munoz and Alexander Isak turned the game in Liverpool's favour and Andrews conceded Yarmoliuk's sending off "changes the dynamics of the game".
To add insult to injury, his side ended the game with nine men after Vitaly Janelt was shown a second yellow card for bringing down Rio Ngumoha on the edge of the penalty area.
"I've seen both of Vitaly's yellows back and where I'm at overall is that I like our players playing with emotion. I think it's a big part of the way we play," he said.

"I like us to play on the edge and, when you do that and you feel like some decisions aren't fair, that can be very, very difficult for our players. I feel it and it can become very, very frustrating. Our players aren't robots.
"I'm more alluding to his first one. I think the second one is about his honesty to get back and chase back towards his own goal, which we have in abundance.
"We have a spirit within this team that I think is really, really special. Most midfielders wouldn't have been able to get back in to even challenge it.
"Could there have been a bit more common sense with the second yellow? I think so."
Iraola: VAR shouldn't have intervened on Liverpool penalty
Iraola, meanwhile, felt the officials were wrong to overturn the Liverpool penalty award before Lewis-Potter's Brentford opener.

Iraola agreed that Dango Ouattara touched the ball while challenging Alexis Mac Allister but insisted VAR should not have intervened, as was the case for Nottingham Forest's penalty against his side in their 2-2 draw at the City Ground in August.

Alisson was controversially penalised for fouling Neco Williams in that game but the key match incidents panel unanimously agreed that it did not reach the threshold for a VAR check and Iraola feels the same logic should have applied to Saturday's incident.
He said: "I think Dango touches the ball. I don't think it's a penalty. But also I don't think the VAR should intervene in that situation because there is clear contact after.
"I remember in the Nottingham Forest penalty against us this season, where they tell us it's not a penalty, VAR is not going to intervene because there is contact.
"So I think it's a very similar situation. I wouldn't call it a penalty, live.
"I think after watching the replay Dango arrives to touch the ball a little bit. But the way they explained to me the situation against Forest is exactly that one.
"I don't think the VAR should intervene."

articles.headline: Seven-try Connacht beat Saracens in Champions Cup
keyFacts: Connacht defeated Saracens 45-36 with seven tries in their opening Investec Champions Cup pool game at Dexcom Stadium.
Captain Cian Prendergast and fly-half Ciaran Frawley each scored two tries for Connacht during the match.
Saracens missed a potential losing bonus point when Owen Farrell converted wide following Elliot Daly's late try.

Connacht produced a superb attacking performance to beat Saracens in their opening Champions Cup pool game.

Captain Cian Prendergast and fly-half Ciaran Frawley scored two tries apiece as Connacht, third from bottom in the United Rugby Championship table after three games, crossed seven times against the three-time Champions Cup winners at a raucous Dexcom Stadium.
Saracens had the chance to leave with a losing bonus point, but Owen Farrell's conversion attempt after Elliot Daly's late try went wide.
The Prem club had led 12-0 early on with tries from Sione Vaenuku and Noah Caluori.
However, Connacht replied with 19 unanswered points as Prendergast, Cathal Forde and Shamus Hurley-Langton all touched down to put the hosts in front.

Hurley-Langton was sin-binned just before the break and Saracens took advantage almost immediately as Nick Tompkins dummied his way over the line from close range with the clock in the red, meaning an enthralling first half ended 19-19.

Connacht, still with 14 men, scored first in the second period when Bundee Aki set up Prendergast's second, although Saracens' response was swift as Farrell and Daly provided an easy run-in for Rotimi Segun.

Frawley's double and another from replacement Caolin Blade helped Connacht build a 14-point gap, despite centre Vaenuku scoring his second for the visitors, which proved more than enough to see out a hugely impressive victory.
A bonus point eluded Connacht, however, with teams needing to score three or more tries than their opponents to earn one in the pool stage this season.
Elsewhere in Pool Two on Saturday, La Rochelle beat South African side Lions 31-14.
Lions played the match in honour of team-mate Hyron Andrews, who died at the team's hotel on Friday aged 31, with tributes paid to the former Sale Sharks player before kick-off.

articles.headline: Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines remaster rumoured, with leaker insisting it's not a remake
keyFacts: A Reddit user leaked that a remaster of the 2004 game Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines is allegedly in development.
The poster stated that the project is specifically a remaster rather than a remake.
No official remaster has been announced, and the claim remains an unsubstantiated rumor.
body: A remaster of cult 2004 RPG Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines may be in the works.
In a post on the r/GamingLeaksAndRumours subreddit, a user wrote: "I can confirm that it is in the works. NOT a Remake, but a Remaster, with some caveats. That's all I can say".

The poster says they have "previously leaked info on multiple other games", including that Forza Horizon 6 is set in Japan, but of course, all we can do is treat this as an unsubstantiated rumour for now.
Their post follows an earlier thread about a possible Bloodlines remake, which they describe as having "kind of leaked" the news already.
Separately, another post on the subreddit, flagged "Grain of Salt", links to a thread about the band Genitorturers, which was involved with the original soundtrack, mentioning a Bloodlines remake.
No remaster has been announced.
ICYMI, Bloodlines 2 wrapped up development in June with its final post-launch update.
The leaker also describes a "dire situation" in the games industry, saying they "expect many games that are in development right now to not see the light of day".

articles.headline: Which Oregon commits, 2028 recruits are on campus for game vs. Nebraska?
keyFacts: The Oregon Ducks will host at least 15 football recruits and commits on the sideline during Saturday's game against the Nebraska Cornhuskers.
Committed visitors attending the game include 2027 class standouts Rashad Streets, Tae Walden Jr., Toa Satele, and Gus Corsair.
The game is scheduled to kick off on Saturday at 8 p.m. PT and will be broadcast live on Fox.
body: The Oregon Ducks are welcoming back several talented recruits and commits once again this weekend against the Nebraska Cornhuskers . They will hope to give the incoming talent a better show than last week's loss to UCLA.

There are expected to be at least 15 recruits on the sideline for Saturday's game, with the potential for the list to expand. Among those visitors are seven committed players in the 2027 class, highlighted by five-star edge rusher Rashad Streets and four-star athlete Tae Walden Jr.

Streets makes the trip from Raleigh, North Carolina, and is one of Oregon's top commits. So far in his senior season, Streets has compiled 60 tackles, 33.5 tackles for loss, and 13 sacks in seven games at Millbrook High School. He is a top-30 recruit in the country, and he has remained steadfast in his commitment to the Ducks , even being one of the more vocal commits on social media, recruiting other players.

Walden was a splashy add to the class over the summer, as the Ducks pulled off the comeback win in the recruiting race after getting his final official visit. Walden is a star at wideout and corner, and he has the potential to play both sides in Eugene. However, Walden has stayed close with Ole Miss and was on campus for the Rebels' emotional win over LSU, so the Ducks have some competition to contend with.

So far this season, Walden has made 47 catches for 797 yards and nine touchdowns as a receiver, while making 16 tackles and six deflections defensively. This is the first time Walden will be on campus this fall, so the Ducks must do what they can to impress him and keep the Tennessee product roped in to Oregon's process.

Also in attendance, the Ducks will welcome four-star linebacker Toa Satele and four-star offensive lineman Gus Corsair , who is back in Eugene for a second consecutive game. In-state commits Malachi Garlington , George VanSandt and Josh Christensen will also return for another game day visit.

Satele, the No. 1 player from Hawaii in the 2027 class, is another guy who could make an immediate impact next season, and he isn't returning to Eugene alone. Satele's younger brother, Trison, is one of the top defensive linemen in the 2028 class and is already a priority target for the Ducks.

Oregon is also hosting 2028 wideout Jayce Halasz for the second weekend in a row and third game-day visit this season. The Washington recruit is heavily considering the Ducks, and he is returning for a second-straight game after not getting to spend enough time with the Ducks last week because of the early kickoff. He has 19 catches for 431 yards and seven touchdowns this season at Graham-Kapowskin High School.

Another intriguing wideout in the class will make his way to Eugene this weekend, as Quincey Clay, the top player in Idaho, will visit the Ducks for the first time. He saw Oregon in action in Los Angeles against USC, and he left Southern California with an offer from the Ducks. Now, he will visit with the potential to become another big Idaho recruiting win for Dan Lanning , following wins with Kenyon Sadiq and Gatlin Bair .

The Ducks are closely linked to 2028 quarterbacks Josiah Boyd and Tristin Gaines , but they are keeping their options open, hosting four-star quarterback Luke Rubley from Aurora, Colorado. A 6-foot-3 passer, Rubley has tossed 15 touchdowns against six interceptions this season, while completing 60.6% of his passes.

Oregon will also host four-star offensive lineman Grayson Williams and four-star defensive lineman Geraci Carson, both of whom are top-100 players in the 2028 class from the Southeast. Carson is a big target in an area the Ducks didn't recruit well in the 2027 class, but LSU and Ole Miss are currently top contenders for the Mississippi recruit. Also, 2029 offensive tackle Sonny Lefotu and his brother, 2028 linebacker Isaiah Lefotu, will both visit from Bakersfield.
Oregon and Nebraska are set to kick off on Saturday at 8 p.m. PT, with the game airing live on Fox.

articles.headline: Newcastle 0-1 Aston Villa: Premier League – live reaction
keyFacts: Aston Villa defeated Newcastle 1-0 in the Premier League after a header from Johan Manzambi.
The victory moved Aston Villa up to 12th place in the league table.
Aston Villa defender Aaron Wan-Bissaka limped off the field during the match with an apparent hamstring injury.
body: Unai Emery is doing it again. Aston Villa have won four of the last five in all competitions and look set for another good season despite losing so many star players in the summer.

Johan Manzanbi, who almost joined Newcastle, headed the winner to lift Villa up to 12th in the table. Newcastle are above them on goals scored but, on this evidence, their rebuild could take longer than Villa’s.

85 min: Big chance for Nwwcastle! Wissa runs at a backpedalling Villa defence, all the way into the area. He has Barnes in a great position to his right but goes for goal himself and shoots just wide. That was a terrific chance.

77 min: Villa substitution Villa’s problems at left-back just got worse: Aaron Wan-Bissaka has limped off to be replaced by Pau Torres. Looks like a hamstring injury, and a pretty bad one because he’s being helped from the field.

74 min: Fine save by Hornicek! Jackson runs at Botman in the area and has a shot blocked. The ball rebounds to Barkley, who cuts across an excellent drive from 25 yards. Hornicek plunges to his right to push it round the post; that’s an excellent stop.

73 min “I could never really decide about Nichlas Jackson at Chelsea - he seemed to get into good positions a lot, with limited end product and a propensity to pick up daft cards,” writes Benjamin Gravestock. “Am increasingly convinced he might actually be the real deal, though. Biggest compliment to him is that we aren’t really missing Ollie Watkins.

“I was among those who thought that Emi Martinez’ time to move on was probably right, even last year; I was hoping for James Trafford, but am extremely happy the club secured Suzuki. Whisper it, but both Jackson and Suzuki might actually be upgrades…”
Jackson could be more ruthless, I guess, but his movement and link play are superb. And you’d imagine that, like Watkins, he’ll only improve under Emery.
72 min: Triple substitution for Aston Villa Ross Barkley, Leon Goretzka and Ibrahim Mbaye replace Emi Buendia, Joao Gomes and the goalscorer Johan Manzambi.,

69 min Barnes’ first-time shot from distance is well blocked on the edge of the D. Moments later, Miley’s cross is headed up in the air towards Wissa, whose sweetly struck scissor-kick is crucially blocked on the six-yard line.

Gonzalez’s free-kick from the right is headed away as far as Wissa on the edge of the area. He’s challenged by a Villa player but Botman smashes a shot on the half turn that is superbly tipped round by the diving Suzuki. Very good save.

47 min “Evening Rob,” writes Simon McMahon. “In another convoluted attempt to shoehorn Dundee United into the Guardian liveblog, daughter Evie and partner Ryan are in Seville tonight, watching Real Betis play Barcelona in La Liga. 2-1 to Barca at half time, Lamine Yamal and Rodri on the scoresheet. Maybe Betis should bring on John Clark and Iain Ferguson at the break, I’ve no doubt Evie will be lecturing the locals on United’s record v Barcelona in Europe, not least to deflect from the current side’s failure to beat St. Johnstone in Perth today...”
That tackle from Sven Botman on Nicolas Jackson looks worse every time you see it – “a disgraceful challenge”, in the words of Jamie Redknapp on Sky Sports.
Apparently the VAR, Stuart Attwell, decided it was reckless rather than dangerous.

“Hmmm, not great watching from an Matthias Jaissle fan club perspective,” writes Chris Paraskevas. “Joelinton hasn’t had the desired effect of shoring up our midfield, which is frequently wide open while trying to play a bizarrely high line against Nicolas Jackson, who thrives off playing off the shoulder.
“The interesting thing is that there are genuine options on the bench: Dedic, Steur, Osula, Toure, Burn and Murphy can all possess their own unique qualities.
“A big issue for MJ is that no-one out there looks like a bona-fide match winner in the Bruno G, Athony G or The Other Bloke mould: the scaling back on proven quality has been sudden and substantial.
“So, it hasn’t quite turned out as it said it would in the brochure, but simultaneously... it’s not as if MJ is inhereting a poor squad.

The half-time whistles brings a short chorus of boos from the home fans. Villa have been the sharper, smarter team and lead through a forceful header from Johan Manzambi, a player Newcastle thought they were going to sign in the summer. Emi Buendia hit the post and Nicolas Jackson, a constant threat on the break, passed up a couple of chances. Newcastle have a lot of work to do.

45 min A reminder that Villa lost more than half the XI that started last season’s Europa League final. I thought it would take Unai Emery a full season to build an effective new side; instead, it looks like he’s done it before the clocks go back.

42 min Barnes stumbles into the six-yard box, forcing Suzuki into a slightly ungainly clearance with his right foot. There was a risk of a ricochet off Barnes and back into the net, but Suzuki got away with it.
Moments later Jackson loses his footing on the edge of the area after another very dangerous break.

Newcastle are all over the show. Wan-Bissaka finds Jackson, who teases a defender on the left side of the area before pushing the ball back to Buendia. He takes a quick touch and rattles a low shot that takes a deflection, hits the inside of the post and ricochets onto the back of the diving Hornicek. Thankfully for Newcastle the ball drops kindly and is cleared.

articles.headline: Liverpool's Florian Wirtz challenge: Do nine chances created in 2-1 win outweigh being physically overmatched?
keyFacts: Florian Wirtz created nine chances during Liverpool's 2-1 win, bringing his season total to a league-leading 20 chances.
Critics argue that Wirtz is easily physically overwhelmed in the Premier League, recording an 11.1% success rate in duels against Brentford.
Data models and analysts showed that many of Wirtz's created chances came from sideways or backwards passes with low expected assist values.
body: LONDON -- Florian Wirtz's critics probably have a point. For $135 million, you probably don't want a player who is so easily physically overwhelmed, who seems utterly out of step with the needs of the modern Premier League. You want a player who can grab a contest from the off and bend it to his will.

Wirtz is yet to do that. Given that the problems that plague him in year two are much the same as 12 months ago, it is valid to ask whether it is ever going to click for Liverpool and the man who was supposed to be the totem of his possession play. Whatever he changes, Wirtz isn't going to gain a couple of inches in height or tack on the half dozen kilos that would get him around league average weight for his position.

In the biggest, strongest and most athletic football league in the world, there is always going to be an opponent who can rag doll him like Brentford did today, where Wirtz put up an 11.1% success rate in duels. When he and his teammates were convinced he should have had a penalty in the first half, it was hard to shake the sense that a stronger player than Wirtz would have held Yehor Yarmolyuk on his shoulder, at least getting a cut back away before going to ground and appealing.

There are reasons why Wirtz is the joint-leader for fouls committed in the Premier League. Sasa Lukic has committed 14 because he is the defensive midfielder for an Ipswich side that generally finds itself on the back foot, needing to throw a boot in the way of danger. Liverpool's No.7 is level with him partly because he is an intense presser but also because when he catches up to the ball (or tries to retain control of it) he finds that the best way to win his possession battle is to go in harder than the other guy. Then again, there is another metric where Wirtz leads the league, the sort you might expect from an eight-figure creator.

Wirtz's supporters probably have a point. After all, no one has laid on more shooting opportunities for his teammates than his 20, albeit that is a number that comes with an awful lot of caveats. Firstly, at this stage of the season it really helps if you have played one more game than a fair few others across the league. And of course, when one game accounts for nearly 15% of your dataset (and half of that match sees you playing with a man advantage), it can have a disproportionate impact on the aggregate.

And so Wirtz tops the creative chart with 20 chances created across the season because he laid on nine today, five in the second half after Yehor Yarmoliuk's headbutt on the impressive Jeremy Jacquet. Not since Bruno Fernandes laid on 10 against Aston Villa in 2021 has a player played more passes in the Premier League that directly result in a teammate taking a shot on goal.

You would think then that this was the day where Wirtz, so roundly chastised for his showing against Manchester City, did what Liverpool have been waiting for: grabbing hold of a game and affirming his status as one of the outstanding creators in the league. Well, not so much. Of those nine chances created, seven came from sideways or backwards passes.

There is value to these and credit should go to a player who knows when his best bet is to move possession on. Just how much value you might ascribe rather depends on the prism you look through. The expected assists (xA) value of the 64 passes Wirtz attempted was just 0.19, less than Dominik Szoboszlai put up in the 32 minutes before he was substituted with an injury. The nine chances Wirtz created had a combined expected goal (xG) tally of around 0.53, nothing to be sniffed at at all. Opta's expected possession value model, which rates the value of every action on the field, said Wirtz was comfortably Liverpool's most effective player.
That initial hit of nine chances created screams "get carried away". The other metrics want you to hold your horses.

Even Andoni Iraola's praise for Wirtz came with the caveat that he had to share the spotlight with the sparky Rio Ngumoha and goalscorer Victor Munoz. "There are very few spaces, small pockets and [very little] time on the ball," he said. "You have to find delicate things because Brentford is a team that defends the box really, really well. You need players like Flo, Rio, Victor was lovely as a right back."

For the most part, this was not Leverkusen Wirtz, gliding into pockets of space, driving beyond the last man to attack the box and either play the final pass or score. Liverpool might never see Leverkusen Wirtz. The athletic standards in the league are too high. Under Iraola, they are not going to play the steady press and possess game with which Xabi Alonso shook the Bundesliga. Liverpool don't have a left back as tactically cute as Alejandro Grimaldo and don't play a back three system that affords quite the same security to their attackers.

A 0.37 xA, 0.31 non-penalty xG, nearly three shots per 90 Wirtz in the Premier League needs too much to change at Liverpool and in the competition as a whole. That doesn't mean that the Wirtz Liverpool have cannot bend a game in moments. Moments such as the fizzing through ball into the path of Munoz, one which the Spaniard took on in stride before chopping in and striking the equaliser on his left foot.

That got Wirtz his assist. He wouldn't have got much on a box score when, dropping off the front line, he flicked a perfect first-time ball over his left shoulder and into the path of Alexander Isak in behind. A smart cut back from the No.9 forced Dango Outtarra into a diving tackle on Alexis Mac Allister so unlikely to succeed that you could see why John Brooks' first instinct was penalty. That initial pass from Wirtz is one that only a handful of Premier League playmakers can deliver.

This might have been a performance of a few moments, but more than one of them could have decided the game in Liverpool's favor. GIven how they seemed to be progressing through treacle before Munoz's goal, making 11 men look like 10, it is fair to wonder whether Wirtz might have delivered the decisive moment.

Can Liverpool supporters demand more than flashes from a player who was, even if only for a matter of weeks, their record signing? Should $135 million get you a bar chart where the green pops a bit more in that chart above rather than the mossy, limey, sap greeny collage you see above? Absolutely. Is Liverpool's XI improved by a number 10 who offers 91st percentile chance creation, 83rd percentile shooting? Undoubtedly.

On the evidence both of today and his Liverpool career as a whole, Wirtz is neither a flop nor the man around whom a title winner might coalesce. He is not responsible for his price tag but instead for his performances. Today's, like that of Liverpool as a whole, was just about good enough. Just don't get carried away with the hype, for good or bad.

articles.headline: Billionaires’ tax getting dry-run in California before socialists, AOC hits DC
keyFacts: California's Proposition 40 proposes a one-time five percent surtax on billionaires' wealth to fund healthcare starting in 2027.
Governor Gavin Newsom, Republicans, and tech executives oppose the measure, while Senator Bernie Sanders and labor unions support it.
California voters will decide on the initiative on November 3, which could spur congressional wealth tax legislation if passed.
body: A billionaires’ tax pushed by radical leftists such as Sen. Bernie Sanders on California’s ballot next month — and with “Squad” Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez ready to take the idea national — a furious, freak alliance of enemies has formed to try to kill it.
Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom is locking arms with furious Republicans, Hollywood elites, and Silicon Valley tech titans to crush the Golden State tax hike before it starts.
Proposition 40 would slap a one-time 5% surtax on the wealth of California billionaires and send most of the money to healthcare, to be paid beginning in 2027 in up to five annual installments.
If the tax scheme passes by referendum on the Nov. 3 ballot, it has the potential to kickstart the debate in Congress, or it could even get copied in other high-wealth states.

Sponsored by the powerful Service Employees International Union and United Healthcare Workers West, it is also backed by democratic socialist Sanders (I-Vt.) and comrade Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.), who represents Silicon Valley.

It’s also gotten a boost from advisors to radical leftist Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), and its top individual donor is Saikat Chakrabarti, a former chief of staff to Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY), who gave $201,000. Those two lawmakers, plus Sanders, are behind efforts in Congress to try to tax billionaires’ wealth.

“It’s a blueprint for direct democracy in the states to retake their power and address some of the actions by Congress,” said Robert Dempsey, San Francisco-based political director of the Sanders-linked Our Revolution, which is pushing the proposal, venting about 2025 Medicaid cuts.
“When leaders don’t lead, the people will hold them accountable. This transcends partisanship,” he warned.

A Mason-Dixon poll last month found support for the measure leading 48% to 39%, with 14% undecided. The proposal has since come under a barrage of attack ads — not only from potential White House hopeful Newsom — but from Democratic gubernatorial candidate Xavier Becerra and Republican Steven Hilton.
Becerra called it “sketchy” and Hilton called it an “insider swamp game” that endangers the economy. The “no” votes were leading by 50-35 in a Manhattan Institute poll early this month.

Newsom has argued that a wealth tax could put California at a disadvantage as some billionaires consider leaving the state. He has instead voiced support for a national approach to taxing billionaire wealth, while arguing that state lawmakers — not a ballot initiative — should decide how California spends its money.

There are already multiple bills in the hopper in Congress to go after billionaires and the rich, with versions by Sanders and Khanna that resemble Prop 40, one by Warren and Rep. Pramila Jayapal (D-WA) to tax “ultra-millionaires,” and more sure to follow with a new crop of DSA lawmakers set to join the House.
Also trashing the proposal are Planned Parenthood and the powerful California Teachers Association union, since it directs the estimated $100 billion money haul toward healthcare instead of schools.

Billionaire Google cofounder Sergey Brin has spent more than $100 million blasting the proposal on the airwaves.
Pollster Brad Coker of Mason Dixon was perplexed that 19% of Republicans supported Prop 40 in his longtime firm’s poll.
“I just couldn’t explain it,” he told The Post.

One theory: the Democratic opposition playing out on California airwaves could be causing a reaction. “What if these guys are voting for it because the Hollywood crowd’s objecting to it all of a sudden,” he said.
Coker also cautioned that voters who remain undecided late in a ballot campaign tend to break against initiatives — a pattern that could pose a challenge for Proposition 40.

articles.headline: iPhone Duo shipping estimates have already been pushed back to 2027
keyFacts: Apple stated that early demand for its new iPhone Duo foldable phone was extraordinary after preorders went live.
Shipping estimates for US preorders have been delayed until January 2027, missing the holiday window.
Apple stated it is working to deliver the product quickly and continues to accept online orders.
body: iPhone Duo shipping estimates have already been pushed back to 2027
Apple called the early demand “nothing short of extraordinary.”

While preorder buzz isn't a solid indication of a device's lasting success, the iPhone Duo has cleared a major early hurdle. After preorders for Apple's first foldable phone went live on Friday, the company characterized the demand as "nothing short of extraordinary" in a statement to CNBC.

So far, shipping estimates for the latest iPhone Duo preorders in the US have been pushed back as late as January 2027. That's bad news for anyone hoping to secure Apple's foldable for the holiday window, but Apple told CNBC that it's "working hard to get this revolutionary new product into customers' hands as quickly as possible, and we will continue accepting orders online."

Anecdotal evidence from online customers are showing everything from being able to pick up their iPhone Duo orders at an Apple Store as early as October 23 to others receiving shipping estimates for November and December. Those who missed the boat on the earliest waves of preorders are seeing delivery windows for January on the online Apple Store, but also a pickup option that says to "Check back for availability on 10.24." Apple has previously mentioned "shopping in-store or online for iPhone Duo," but hasn't confirmed if its physical locations or other authorized retailers would have in-store stock. As for third-party options, Best Buy's website is currently showing iPhone Duo shipping estimates for November as of the time of the article's publishing.

articles.headline: Zelensky says Starshield still restricted in Ukraine as Musk and White House refuse to take responsibility
keyFacts: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that SpaceX's Starshield systems remain restricted in Ukraine while working properly in neighboring European Union countries.
Zelensky claimed the restrictions are a planned operation targeting Kyiv, though U.S. officials and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk denied throttling the system.
Ukraine uses Starshield for drone strikes and air defense, and the disruptions follow U.S. warnings against striking Russian oil refineries.
body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Saturday said Starshield systems are still being restricted for use in his country’s war against Russia, warning the breakdown is a “planned operation” to target Kyiv.

Starshield is SpaceX ‘s military version of Starlink that the company says is owned and operated by the U.S. government. Ukraine has been using Starshield to boost its drone strike missions and air defenses against Russia, but announced on Wednesday that the system is being newly restricted, four days after Trump called for new leadership in Kyiv, contending that Zelensky is unable to agree to a peace deal ending the war.

Zelensky has expressed intense concern that throttling Starshield is hindering Kyiv’s fight against Russia. He said on Saturday that Ukraine tested and confirmed that Starshield “worked perfectly” in adjacent European Union countries. The Ukrainian president suggested that the speed limit is a deliberate choice despite U.S. officials and SpaceX telling the Ukrainian government at several levels that the problem is “technical issues.”

“We have the relevant logs and evidence to prove this,” Zelensky said. “The conclusion is clear: the restrictions are in effect within Ukraine but do not apply within the European Union. In other words, this is a planned operation.”

Both the United States and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk have denied they are throttling Starshield and claimed ignorance about why the system is down. Reports suggest the move was initially suggested by Musk but decided by Trump.

Starshield is a defense communications system that helps to track and intercept incoming threats, in addition to helping carry out strikes. Ukraine uses the system to help guide drones to Russian targets and protect its own skies.

Zelensky said earlier this week that starting overnight on Tuesday, Starshield was no longer working for drones moving roughly 100 miles per hour. On Saturday, he said that when tested in other countries, the system worked perfectly for speeds exceeding 111 miles per hour. To make up the difference, Zelensky said Saturday that Ukraine is turning to fighter jets to intercept drones, with a success rate of around 50%.
He said Ukraine “can’t use Starlink or Starshield technology on our territory today to shoot down jet-powered Shaheds.”
“They fly, and we can stop them with aircraft and other air defense, but we don’t use Starlink for that, unfortunately. God willing, this will be restored,” Zelensky said.

Zelensky said Wednesday during an interview on Piers Morgan Uncensored that he hoped the restriction was only a “mistake” and perhaps “a huge technical problem” at SpaceX. But he suggested the truth lay elsewhere.
“They knew what they did,” Zelensky said, referring to SpaceX and the U.S.

The Starshield disruptions come shortly after the U.S. expressed anger that Ukraine is carrying out strikes against Russian oil refineries, which Trump is relying upon to help mitigate surging energy prices caused by the Ukraine and Iran wars.

“We said you can do whatever you want to Russia , [but] don’t hit the refineries because that’s a world problem,” Trump said of Zelensky earlier this month. “He wants to make problems for our farmers, our ranchers, with diesel fuel because Russia supplies a large portion of the diesel fuel throughout the world, and we told them, do whatever you want, but don’t hit the diesel fuel because there’s a big problem, a big shortage. And what does he do? He goes and hits the diesel fuel.”

articles.headline: The Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Sounds Meaningfully Better Than the Original
keyFacts: Nintendo executive Bill van Zyll stated that the company remains committed to supporting physical media and cartridges for platforms like the Switch 2.
Polygon reported that the upcoming Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake feels snappy, streamlined, and polished, addressing the sluggish frame rate of the original N64 version.
Previewers noted that the Ocarina of Time remake appears to have been developed by one of Nintendo's internal teams, resulting in responsive gameplay and improved visuals.
body: Switchboard is Polygon's weekly newsletter for all things Nintendo, sent on Thursdays and published on the site on Saturdays. You can subscribe here.

Guess what — Nintendo's all-in on physical media. This unsurprising fact became news this week after an executive for Nintendo in Latin America made some mild and extremely uncontroversial comments to the effect. "We know how much the fans like it," Bill van Zyll said, while pointing out that the company had just launched a new platform, in Switch 2, that supports physical cartridges. This is only worth noting due to Sony's unpopular decision to end production of physical PlayStation games starting in 2028, but still: good to know.

As a family-oriented company which still has strong ties to toy retail, Nintendo enjoys a far higher proportion of physical retail sales than any of its competitors, so this position just makes a boring kind of sense. But it also has more to lose; as pressure on memory chip prices continues, Switch game cards are surely much more expensive to manufacture than Blu-ray discs. Hence the functionally empty game-key cards most third-party publishers have resorted to. But when it comes to its own titles, Nintendo still insists on shipping the full game on the card, and hang the expense.

You can tell what matters to Nintendo by what it chooses to spend money on. It typically doesn't go overboard on development budgets for its games, reasoning that expensive graphical fidelity won't add a proportional amount of fun. (It would also take up more of those costly gigabytes). But Nintendo goes out of pocket to put all of, say, next month's Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on a game card, because it is a proportionally better experience. Imagine being nine years old, unwrapping the game for Christmas, putting it in your Switch 2 and then having to wait for it to download. Unacceptable.

First hands-on impressions of the Ocarina remake were published this week, and Polygon's Michael McWhertor found it "snappy, streamlined, and polished in ways that make it feel totally fresh." Here again, Nintendo's priorities are instructive.
Nintendo has revisited this game several times before, but this time is different.

The 3DS' Ocarina of Time 3D was handed to an external team, Grezzo, as was the pretty but laggy 2019 remake of Link's Awakening. But Ocarina 2026, unlike its sister N64-era remake Star Fox, appears to have been allocated to one of Nintendo's precious internal teams, and the difference is apparent. Beyond the lush visuals, previewers all noted how frictionless and responsive the remake is, a huge correction of the biggest historical flaw with one of Nintendo's greatest games. (The original N64 game runs at a sluggish 20 frames per second, and you can really feel it.)

Nintendo has the same cynical reasons for leaning on remakes to pad out the release schedule as every other publisher. Games are risky endeavors, and new ideas are hard to come by. But in this case, it seems Nintendo also saw an opportunity to make a classic game meaningfully better, and — just as with its first-party game cards — refused to take half measures. This is about legacy, about brand reputation. And there's little Nintendo cares about more.
eShop game of the week: Ratatan

The PlayStation Portable cult classic Patapon, a rhythm-action game about a line of little marching warriors, has been reimagined by some of its original developers in a roguelike spiritual sequel. It doesn't quite hang together, but it's a powerful nostalgia trip all the same.
Nintendo Classics game of the week: Castlevania: Bloodlines

As the excellent Castlevania: Belmont's Curse arrives on Switch, it's a good moment to revisit this half-forgotten Sega Genesis entry in the series. It's not the Castlevania you know; instead, it's a perfect, technologically impressive expression of a more straight-ahead action game like the NES originals.
Nintendo Music track of the week: "Guru-Guru's Song" from The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask

The strange, funhouse-mirror atmosphere of Ocarina of Time's direct sequel is captured perfectly by this carnivalesque retread of the "Song of Storms" melody, as if performed by a circus organ-grinder and their monkey.

articles.headline: Crystal Lake review: Peacock's Friday the 13th prequel series is a must-watch this Halloween
keyFacts: The eight-episode prequel series Crystal Lake has been released on Peacock to explore the origins of Pamela Voorhees.
Linda Cardellini stars as Pamela Voorhees alongside Hamish Linklater as Jason's father, Elias, in the horror series penned by Brad Caleb Kane.
International viewers must wait for future release dates according to the scheduling information provided in the review.
body: TechRadar Verdict

Crystal Lake is the perfect TV series to watch this Halloween, as it takes a deep dive into Pamela Voorhees' psyche. Finally, we get to learn more about the Friday the 13th character, played brilliantly by Linda Cardellini.
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.

Friday the 13th's prequel series Crystal Lake has arrived on Peacock, with all eight episodes available to watch. International viewers need to wait a little longer, though; check out our Crystal Lake release date schedule for more on that.

Across eight episodes, Crystal Lake explores the origins of Pamela Voorhees, Jason's mother and the original killer in the popular slasher franchise. I've been excited about this for months, as we haven't really had a deep dive into who Pamela is across the original movie series.

Linda Cardellini stars in the leading role, bringing many layers to Pamela. The catalyst for her behavior comes when her young son, Jason (Callum Vinson), drowns at Camp Crystal Lake, where she works as a cook. Grief-stricken, Pamela struggles to cope, leading to increasing paranoia and an eventual spiral into the serial killer we know her as.

Pamela is shown through a very empathetic lens, as a lonely single mother who has lost her only child. She has everything ripped away from her and even so, tries her best to keep it together. But her descent into insanity is inevitable, and even in the first episode, the kills are brutal and shocking.

There's some mystery surrounding Pamela's past that's well worth sticking around for. In Crystal Lake, Pamela feels really well-rounded, and as a huge fan of the original movies, I loved how much care the creators put into fleshing her out.

Crystal Lake was penned by Brad Caleb Kane, who recently worked on HBO Max's excellent IT series Welcome to Derry. I've really been enjoying his adaptations of classic horror media recently, and I hope it continues.

There's also a welcome expansion on another character. Jason's father, Elias, gets a new storyline that ties in well with Pamela's mysterious backstory. Elias is played by Hamish Linklater, who delivers a great performance as a man whose decisions severely influence how Jason turns out and, crucially, how he actually survives his drowning, as we've seen in the original Friday the 13th movie.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.

Crystal Lake adds a lot of new lore to the franchise, but it does feel like it's stretched out in places. These pacing issues didn't affect my enjoyment of the series too much, but even a six-episode run would've felt tighter, in my opinion.

I hope many Friday the 13th fans share my opinions about Crystal Lake, particularly when it comes to the characters, and how they've been given genuinely interesting backstories and expansions beyond the original movies. This is the kind of prequel that feels like it was made by someone who really cares about the source material.

There are a lot of nods to the movies, such as seeing the killer's point of view, that chilling score, and a title sequence that will make anyone feel nostalgic for the era of 80s slasher films. It's a well-crafted series with great editing, something that fits right in with the abundance of Friday the 13th stories.

In my opinion, this is the perfect series to watch over Halloween, or indeed sooner if you're feeling impatient. It's gripping and binge-worthy, giving horror fans both familiarity and some new material for them to get excited about.

articles.headline: To help America, I used Crusader Kings 3 to figure out how to remove a doddering, senile lunatic from power
keyFacts: A writer used the video game Crusader Kings 3 to figure out how to remove a senile leader from power.
The writer attempted various strategies, including diplomacy, flattery, and war, while dealing with an in-game plague called Wenzel's Cough.
The writer's character ultimately died of illness without succeeding in removing the aging ruler from power.
body: I heard it on the wireless: election fever is sweeping America. The world's loudest democracy is headed to the ballot box to vote in its next slate of soda jerks and Chevrolets and whatever else it is they have over there. It's all very exciting.

Can I help? Yes. I've already solved my own country's politics, now it's time to help the benighted and backward people of places like "Connecticut" and "the Oklahoma Panhandle"—fantasy names from a land beyond knowing. People love it when foreigners tell them how to do their own domestic politics, and especially when they have as robust a methodology as I have: a copy of Crusader Kings 3 and most of the DLC.

Using Paradox's premier 1066 simulator, I will ascertain the best way to remove a burrowed-in leader from power. Which real-life figure is this a videogame analogue for? Don't worry about it, don't email me about it, and don't launch a cruise missile at my house.
Don't email me about how the midterms don't choose the president either. I don't know what those words mean.
King of New York
I first had to create an accurate, 11th-century simulacrum of an American president. None of CK3's historical rulers quite fit the bill, so I decided to create a ruler from scratch.
I created an 80-year-old lecher named Wenzel and put him in charge of the Holy Roman Empire. His defining trait was 'lunatic'.

So that was sorted. Next, I needed a position from which to actually act in the world. I needed to be someone who could effect change in the HRE and test my theories as to the best way to go about removing a leader. This was easier: I simply nosed through Wenzel's myriad direct vassals and picked one who seemed most like some guy, thus to represent the working masses of the American Empire. I've quite genuinely forgotten his name, but he had very few traits and was prone to tuberculosis.
